daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

The controversy over Vice President Gibran's educational credentials intensified as lawyer Denny Indrayana called for impeachment proceedings, arguing that Gibran no longer meets the constitutional requirements for vice president. The dispute has sparked inter-party tensions between Demokrat and PSI politicians, with Demokrat leader AHY being drawn into the debate. Denny Indrayana outlined five steps his group plans to take following a recent court decision on Gibran's high school certificate, while UNS alumni withdrew their lawsuit at the Constitutional Court regarding high school diploma requirements for presidential and vice-presidential candidates.

  • Vice President Gibran visited West Sulawesi schools and hospitals, urging residents not to believe hoaxes during his regional tour.
  • National Police Chief dismissed the Sukoharjo police chief following the controversial raid on Ponpes Hamalatul Quran, a decision welcomed by the MUI.
  • A cassava trader from Pekalongan was named a suspect in connection with the October 28 demonstration, with his family called to Bareskrim for questioning.
  • Police seized Rp 980 million in counterfeit money allegedly intended to finance demonstrations in Jakarta, with the owner promised Rp 300 million.
  • Women's Empowerment Minister requested a review of the new tax on sanitary pads.
  • AKBP Netty Rosdiana resigned from the National Police.
  • National Police guaranteed no special treatment for AKBP Edy Herwiyanto, father of Kediri's mayor.

Foreign Policy & Defence

Indonesian police named 13 suspects in a human trafficking case involving Indonesians recruited as mercenaries for Russia's military. The suspects allegedly recruited Indonesian citizens of various ages with promises of Rp 400 million contracts and Rp 50 million monthly salaries, plus child allowances, sending them to the battlefield after only one month of training. The case highlights indiscriminate age recruitment practices in the trafficking operation.

  • Indonesian and Swiss officials strengthened cooperation in sovereign AI development.
  • Indonesia's Foreign Minister discussed a comprehensive partnership with France's foreign minister on the sidelines of the G20 summit in Atlanta.
  • UN Secretary-General candidate Lana Nusseibeh praised Indonesia as a driver of multilateralism.
  • An expert suggested that Indonesia should review its BoP membership following elections in the US and Israel.
  • Indonesia's Education Ministry expanded the internationalization of Indonesian language in Russia.

Other

Indonesia targets Rp 165 trillion in mineral and coal revenue by year-end 2026, as the government focuses on resource sector earnings. The government also urged nickel producers to reduce output in response to falling global prices, while simultaneously working to build an integrated nickel downstreaming industry.

  • The Maha gas field began production, adding to Indonesia's national gas supply.
  • Transportation operators were instructed to prepare operational plans for the 2026/2027 year-end holiday season, with safety as the minister's top priority.
  • Bank Indonesia hailed September's trade surplus as an economic buffer.
  • The KPK is open to summoning Ahmad Dhani after court hearings revealed he requested customs officials' help with detained goods, with witness Ferry detailing Febrie Adriansyah's money requests in the Jiwasraya case.
  • Indonesia allocated Rp 2.6 trillion to subsidize microloans for women.
